documents.title: Hematology clinic letter
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Adult Sickle Cell Program. Clinic date 02/25/2025.

Dear Dr. (primary care),
Curtis returns for routine review. Interval history notable for laparoscopic cholecystectomy in November complicated by an intraoperative malignant hyperthermia reaction; he recovered fully and we have flagged MH susceptibility in our records. No pain admissions. He continues hydroxyurea most days and folic acid daily.
Exam: well, mild icterus, no hepatosplenomegaly, no leg ulcers.
Labs today at his steady state.

Plan: continue hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily and folic acid 1 mg daily. CBC and retic every 3 months. Any future procedure requiring anesthesia should involve us in advance. Return in 6 months.
Allergies: NKDA. MH susceptible: avoid volatile anesthetics and succinylcholine.

With thanks,
Hematology attending

events.reason: left flank pain and blood in urine

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Indication: left flank pain, gross hematuria, sickle cell disease.
Technique: CT of the abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast, including excretory phase images.
Findings: Left kidney is normal in size. On excretory images, contrast extends from the calyx into a left renal papilla, forming a small cavity at the papillary tip, consistent with papillary necrosis. No renal or ureteral calculus. No hydronephrosis or perinephric fluid. Right kidney enhances and excretes normally with no papillary abnormality. Bladder unremarkable. Gallbladder surgically absent. Liver, pancreas and adrenals unremarkable. No free fluid. Bowel normal in caliber. No lymphadenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Findings of left renal papillary necrosis. No urolithiasis or obstruction.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED. Date of service 05/14/2025.

HPI: 22-year-old man with HbSS sickle cell disease and a history of malignant hyperthermia during surgery last year, here for two days of left-sided flank pain with visibly bloody urine. No injury, no recent heavy exertion. No fever, no dysuria. He is vague about family history and mentions his father has some kind of blood problem.
Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily (taken intermittently per hematology), albuterol HFA 2 puffs q4-6h prn wheeze, folic acid 1 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA. MH susceptible.
Social: never smoker; alcohol 1-2 drinks per month; student and part-time retail.

Exam: T 37.2, BP 130/80, HR 88, RR 16. Uncomfortable but nontoxic. Mild tenderness over the left CVA. Abdomen soft, no guarding, no rebound. No suprapubic tenderness.

Results: Urinalysis negative for leukocyte esterase and nitrite, large blood, RBC too numerous to count, red cell casts seen on microscopy. Creatinine and BUN within normal range. CT abdomen/pelvis with excretory phase: left papillary necrosis, no stone, no obstruction.

ED course and impression: renal papillary necrosis, left, in the setting of sickle cell disease. Pain controlled with IV fluids and acetaminophen. Discharged home.
Instructions: drink plenty of fluids; acetaminophen for pain; avoid ibuprofen, naproxen and other NSAIDs; follow up with primary care within 1 week and inform hematology; return for fever, clots or inability to urinate, or worsening pain.

documents.title: ER visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Went to the ER wed night for pain in my left side and my pee was red. they did a CT and said it was papillary necrosis in my kidney from the sickle cell. said to see you this week or next. urine is lighter now.

documents.title: RE: ER visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks Curtis. Front desk will set up a visit for next week. Keep up the fluids, use acetaminophen only (no ibuprofen or naproxen), and let your hematology team know. If the bleeding gets heavy, you pass clots, can't pee, or get a fever, go back to the ER. We are requesting the ER record.

documents.title: Office Visit: post-ED
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED visit 5/14 for left flank pain and gross hematuria; told papillary necrosis on CT (ED record requested, not yet here, history per patient and his discharge sheet).
Now: flank pain gone since about the weekend. Urine looks normal to him for 3 days. No fever, no clots, no burning. Has been drinking a lot of water. Used acetaminophen only. Messaged hematology.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. No CVA tenderness either side. Abdomen soft.
UA in office: small blood, 8 RBC/hpf, protein negative, LE and nitrite negative.

A/P
1. Renal papillary necrosis, left, from sickle cell disease. Clinically settling; residual microscopic blood expected for a while. Recheck urine at his physical. Strict NSAID avoidance, reviewed again, including combination cold products. Stay well hydrated, especially during work shifts. Return precautions given.
2. HbSS, MH susceptibility, asthma: unchanged.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. Starting his last year of school in a couple weeks.
Since May: no further flank pain or red urine. No admissions. Saw hematology in Feb; says he went again this month but we have no letter. Hydroxyurea still most days, folic acid daily. Albuterol rarely, mostly spring.
Allergy list: NKDA; MH-susceptible alert in place. He got the medical alert bracelet and is wearing it today.
Family: parents with sickle trait; maternal uncle with suspected MH; paternal grandmother asthma.
Social: never smoker, occasional drink.

ROS negative.
Exam: vitals as charted. Mild icterus. Heart: soft flow murmur, unchanged. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed port scars. No CVA tenderness. Legs without ulcers.

A/P
- Renal papillary necrosis, left (May): UA today negative for blood. Continue NSAID avoidance.
- HbSS on hydroxyurea: CBC, retic, CMP drawn; copies to hematology. Will request their August note.
- MH susceptibility: alert reviewed.
- Mild intermittent asthma: no change.
- Vaccines: flu and COVID once available this fall. PHQ-2 1.
One year.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Curtis, urine is clear of blood now, which is what I hoped to see. Blood counts and chemistries are in your normal range for HbSS. Good luck with the semester.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from his apartment, identity checked by name and DOB.
Store wants a form for holiday hours and he is down to his last inhaler. Breathing fine, albuterol maybe once a month. No night cough. No sickle pain since spring, urine normal.
Appears comfortable, no audible wheeze, speaking easily.
A/P: mild intermittent asthma, stable; albuterol renewed. Work form signed, no restrictions. Due for physical next summer.
